pieces.name: Foundation
pieces.bar: Not a GDD bar — infrastructure. Must render, screenshot, and test.
pieces.note: Expo + TS strict + vitest + Skia-on-web + Playwright screenshot harness all verified working end to end.

pieces.name: RPE → %1RM table
pieces.bar: Published RPE charts. Binary and testable — critic verifies against source values.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR after six rounds. The final critic re-fetched both sources live at the pinned SHAs and confirmed every sampled cell matches the bytes, that the one documented disagreement is real and exactly where the module says it is, that no export remains mutable, that no indexed read can leak undefined past a null check, and that the hot path is unchanged. It named two stale-prose residuals and explicitly said not to spawn a round for them — folded into this touch instead. The chart still cannot be checked against the RTS publication from here, and the module claims no more than that.

pieces.name: e1RM formulas
pieces.bar: Published e1RM formulas. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: THE MATH WINS ITS BAR. The critic verified the Epley divisor against published sources and a pinned third-party implementation, re-fetched both chart fixtures and confirmed every cell the boundary figures depend on, hand-checked all five worked examples and the crossover point, confirmed the curve is strictly increasing across the whole domain and that the refusal fires exactly where the chart’s coverage ends, and found no invented value anywhere. All seven §12.3 conditions clean. Its one finding was a false quotation of CLAUDE.md in the module header — correct that the quote was false, but wrong about how: git history shows the phrase WAS in CLAUDE.md when the builder quoted it, and I removed it two commits later without updating the quotation. My staleness, not a fabrication. Fixed by quoting the rule as it now stands, verified verbatim against the flattened file.

pieces.name: DOTS scoring
pieces.bar: Published DOTS coefficients. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: MERGED. Every DOTS value used to be asserted against ITSELF, so a digit transposed at authoring time gave a self-consistent wrong answer with a green suite; the critic had caught the current coefficients by going outside the repo BY HAND and nothing made the next reader do that. Now 26 committed rows verified against three external implementations the builder FETCHED AND RAN locally rather than transcribed, with all ten coefficients mutation-tested one at a time: 10/10 caught at 1e-12 relative. Three of my brief claims falsified by measurement and all reported: there are NO turning points inside the domain to sample near (the real roots sit at ~228.8kg and ~153.6kg, outside the clamps, which looks like why the clamps are where they are); 2-dp published tables CANNOT support the required sensitivity, because at 0.005 seven of the ten last-digit mutations are invisible; and single transposed digit spans six orders of magnitude and is not one claim. It also found a pre-existing overstatement in the dots.test.ts header - the Python reference it credited was fed the same ten in-repo numbers, so it proved term order and not provenance. Limit recorded rather than glossed: no published TABLE of scores is reachable from this sandbox, so the fixture is the output of external code, and two of the three sources declare descent from the same crate.

pieces.name: Meet engine
pieces.bar: Meet structure correctness: order, 3 attempts, non-decreasing weight, best-per-lift total, bomb-out.
pieces.note: Structure WINS ITS BAR. Rework 5 merged: the rules-seal subsystem is gone — four constants, a unique-symbol brand, an error code, an exported check, four call sites, a 41-line essay and nine tests, including the BigInt re-derivation blind to the digits it was meant to check. Rules are now opaque behind a module-private symbol, so the tampering spread does not type-check, and the guard is proven by negative controls that revert it and confirm the directives go unused. meet.ts is 51 lines shorter and has no arithmetic left to get wrong.

pieces.name: Fatigue / readiness
pieces.bar: Plausible game-feel abstraction. No visible fatigue meter (§12.3).
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR. The critic had cleared the model and both live §12.3 refusal conditions, re-deriving the daily-vs-intermittent injury comparison by hand rather than taking the claim; what it sent back was two tests that could not fail if the behaviour they named were deleted. Both are now fixed and I re-ran the mutations myself rather than accepting the report: delete the technique-relief term and 1 test fails where 0 did before; delete physio shortening and 2 fail where 0 did. The technique test now pins the exact scaling across six ratings instead of asserting probability > 0, and physio is compared against the same duration roll unaided instead of restating a band the unaided value already satisfied. The third, weaker case was given real content rather than deleted, and the builder proved that by mutation too. Model untouched throughout.

pieces.name: Streak / Recovery Days
pieces.bar: Never punishes daily engagement. Manual token use, hold cap, first-break tutorial.
pieces.note: CLOSED BY THE HUMAN after four rulings. The monotonicity defect is gone at the root: idle days are charged on BOTH sides of a run, so the asymmetry that made training one more day end on a lower streak has no side to live on. Recovery Days as a stock became a ROLLING ENTITLEMENT - COVERED_DAYS_PER_WINDOW per WINDOW_DAYS - and the burn takes everything left rather than a debit, because "take everything left" is the only consumption idempotent under splitting a window. 0 violations across every funding source and horizon tested, and the human insisted that 0 be treated as a HYPOTHESIS: lifetime-best monotonicity at 40/60/80/100 days, deficit MAGNITUDE not just frequency at 60/100/400, multiple income parameterisations. The 8.3E Extra Covered Day purchase ships with training-funded currency STRUCTURALLY unable to reach it - a provenance split keyed on the ARRIVAL rather than the tender, so both banned tenders collapse to one row - not merely empirically clean. The store refuses to sell during an already-doomed absence, with a player-facing message rather than a dead button, and both directions tested because the false-positive direction is the one that hides a bug. Sale completion re-validates against live settled state, extended through the existing 98,304-decision equivalence suite rather than pinned by a one-off.

pieces.name: Tuning constants
pieces.bar: Every game-feel value a named constant in one place. Enforced by a magic-number audit.
pieces.note: THE COMMENT SCANNER IS A SCAN NOW, AND THE BLIND SPOT IS CLOSED. The two substitution regexes are gone; withoutComments and onlyComments are views of one hand-written pass, so the pair partitions any input BY CONSTRUCTION. THE_PARSER_DISAGREES_HERE is empty, with the old substitution kept in the test as a known-wrong stream so the empty list is a MEASUREMENT rather than an absence. Three contradictions of my brief, all right. It DID NOT use ts.createSourceFile as the implementation, and the reason is better than my instruction: the test oracle IS that parser, so using it in the implementation would make the strongest assertion in the file compare the parser to itself. It measured the hand-written walk against the parser over all 170 files instead - 0 missed, 0 over-claimed, 0 partition failures. My 54-runs figure was true of the RUNS and hid most of the defect: 54-56 runs but 26,734 CHARACTERS across 23 files, 20,612 in one file. And the bug also silently GAINS code, which is the larger number. THE HOLE DEMONSTRATED END TO END: the banned architectural claim planted on a line containing a glob goes red under the new scanner, and under the old substitution the same claim sitting in the same file passes 39/39.

pieces.name: Progression boundary
pieces.bar: No client-authoritative progression writes. Shaped for Edge Functions.
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR. The write side already won; the read side now has consumers, and the builder did not just add callers — it removed the bypass. There is no ServerRecord in useSession any more and no accessor for the row, so reaching for the wrong source does not typecheck because the wrong source is gone. All seven accessors went from ZERO non-test callers to real ones. I verified in the browser myself, 25/25 against the running app: server 196.1 on screen against the client own projection of 208.6, PR gold following the server from rgb(255,215,94) to rgb(232,236,244), a refused proposal showing the last confirmed 200.0 rather than the discarded 208.6, and accessory day rendering NO e1RM node at all with an em dash rather than a zero. It also found that projected was UNREACHABLE code before this — the old path proposed and settled inside one state updater, so pending existed as a local variable and never as rendered state, which means a renderer handling that branch would have been untestable decoration. Fatigue narrowed rather than documented: the brief carries exactly one field behind a compile-time allowlist, pruned to §3.4 horizon. Disclosed weakness: the browser verification is not wired into the suite, so a regression there is caught only by running the tool.

pieces.name: Lift input mechanic
pieces.bar: The lift must feel good (GDD pillar 1).
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR, and the brace gap is now closed too. The builder REFUTED the premise I passed it — rung 1 is not too strong for a static hold, it measured 48 silhouette and 252 changed body pixels of 1406 — and then found that the one-number fix I suggested would have made things WORSE: at any brace weight high enough to matter, the lifter popped back to rung 0 on the first tick of the descent, visibly loosening the instant the bar moved. So it moved BRACE and DESCENT_TOP together to 0.42, arguing the brace IS the top of the descent held still, and swept at 0.01 to avoid three values where a rung crossing lands on a depth-step boundary and silently costs a drawing. Brace strain is now 0 for light and 1 for both the default and maximal, and the light brace still reads unstrained. Motion channels byte-identical. Its mutation fails five tests with the pixel check failing at literally 0, not a shrunken number. It also noticed it was editing a constant that exists in TWO files and added a cross-file assertion that they agree, which nothing had enforced.

pieces.name: Lifter sprites & animation
pieces.bar: Blind A/B against real 16-bit sprite work — NOW GRADEABLE, reference committed.
pieces.note: MERGED. @ours now expresses integers and converges on the @ref grammar rather than growing a second dialect; 22 integer entries, six of them DERIVED rather than typed. Two results beyond the fix. M9: emptying the ban file list left the suite GREEN on the builder OWN first cut - it found that itself, named it the vacuity failure GDD §12.2 spends a page on, and fixed it by pinning the list contents AND requiring per listed file that stripping the tags back to bare digits makes the ban fire. M11: it ran the critic concrete scenario for real, moved UPPER_ARM_R, then played the builder until every MEASUREMENT assertion was green - and 55 tagged prose sites then reported themselves falsified, including the exact sentence the critic named. It reports the critic cost estimate was low: four test cases reddened and ELEVEN constant edits were needed, not two. Measured rather than typed: BRACE ASCENT is 135, so the doc figure was right and merely unguarded - the finding was the guard, not the number. Residual, self-declared: OURS_BAN_MIN_INTEGER = 10 is a judgement call from one file evidence, and the ban is value-based so it cannot tell a policed count from a coincidence.

pieces.name: Gym / environment art
pieces.bar: Blind A/B, same era. Readability at phone scale.
pieces.note: MAJORITY-PASS on the training gym, with the MEET VENUE REPORTED AS A FAIL rather than passed. The ruler is honest now: EDGE_LUMA_DELTA 20 is the one authored number and the other two are structural divisions of it, both false mortar claims are deleted, and the anchor is bracketed two-sided off the palette. The three real course deltas - 0.00, 15.09, 8.89 - are pinned TWICE, once off the palette and once off the RENDERED wall, so the comment cannot drift from the renderer again. The flat top band is now a stated decision rather than a missing map entry: WALL_DEEP is the bottom rung and the bank is 16/16 spent, so there is no darker colour to draw a course in. It computed what the anchor would have to be to fail rather than asserting it away - whole-suite headroom is 2.15 luma. THE FAIL: adding a WORST-CASE rim check, because the percentiles are structurally blind below p05, surfaced a 0.00-luma contact between the lifter HAIR_DARK and the crowd CROWD_MID, both at 45.22. The bound is 0, the only one calibrated against nothing, and the meet test asserts the failure by EQUALITY so it cannot grow a second entry. The corrected crowd disclosure is exact: p05 reads the 18th-worst of 358 crossings, so a collision under a twentieth of the silhouette cannot move it however bad it is. Three ceilings planted, three more found that the critic had not named, and the prose claim replaced with a coverage LEDGER that accumulates every bound ever actually failed and asserts it against the bound list. Its first two plants were sized from the bound they test; it caught that itself and re-sized them from the artifact. Best discipline of the round: it built the prop shadow on the dark floor, measured that it took descent rim p25 from 22.15 to 19.37 against a floor of 20, and DID NOT SHIP IT, stating in code that five props still stand on nothing rather than hiding it.

pieces.name: Daily session loop
pieces.bar: Duolingo-class session. Time-to-first-input, session length, close-out moment.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR on everything gradeable. Time-to-first-input and session length pass and are measured at 54.3 to 60.3 seconds, with the floor DROPPED rather than padded. Both human rulings are now honoured in the WORDS as well as the numbers: a primed accessory day reads ACCESSORY BANKED, verified on the running app, where it used to read NEW e1RM over a Training IQ row with no number. The fixture moved from STEADY, the one readiness that arithmetically cannot produce a PR, to PRIMED, with a non-vacuity guard that fails if it is put back. The close-out frames now exist - 12 captured, 27 boundary checks passing. Whether the close-out LANDS is a feel judgement no critic here can make.

pieces.name: Meet day
pieces.bar: Dread and anticipation comparable to a real third-attempt walkout.
pieces.note: FIXED AND MERGED - WITHOUT A BUILDER REPORT. The agent finished eight commits and a clean worktree, then died before reporting: the silent-death pattern this run has recorded twice, where a dead agent looks exactly like a slow one. Everything recorded here I read out of the diff and verified by running it. || THE DEFECT: 48% of a third-attempt walkout was a frozen frame over silence - useHallStep cancelled its rAF at motionMs while the beat ran to 4100ms, and CROWD_SWELL_BIG had decayed by 2520ms. All 2400ms of the three escalation extras landed after every channel had finished, so meetTuning's own instruction to lengthen WALKOUT_MS "here and nowhere else" only ever lengthened dead air. || NOW: buildWalkout sheets the WHOLE beat, beatMs is required, and the tail carries a named BRACE and HUSH - bar bend and tilt and body pitch oscillating, the crowd's standing wave travelling deeper across the brace then holding. A walkout-brace cue plays the bed again, scheduled BACKWARDS from the hush so the room is there while he braces and gone before the bar moves. MEASURED IN A BROWSER on a played third attempt: six changes in the 1180ms tail, 672ms of it drawing, against a beat seen to end at 3149ms. || IT FOUND THREE GAPS IN ITS OWN WORK BY MUTATION, which is what earned the merge with no report to read. The brace-invariance sweep compared bracePhaseAt's own outputs, which take (ms, plan) and cannot see a load ratio - so multiplying the phase by loadRatio inside drawKeyAt left it GREEN; it now compares the DRAWN deltas at every tick. The tail's crowd ramp was pinned only at its endpoints, so doubling its rate passed. And ATTEMPT_SHAPES was missing the one shape whose brace window lands near MIN_BRACE_WINDOW_MS, so deleting that floor changed nothing the sweep could see. || The verdict beat is taken the other way and deliberately: deliberationMs now takes AttemptStakes, verdictMs deliberately does not. || EVERY VALUE IS UNPLAYED. Nobody has heard the new cue or seen the brace at speed. || THE HALL CARRIES THROUGH THE CUT. Dispatched with FREEZE as the recommended route rather than a fourth scan, because every round of this piece has added an instrument a later round found scoped too narrowly, and freezing removes the capability instead of enumerating its uses. || THE COHERENCE PASS FAILED THE BAR, AND THE CAUSE IS ONE MISSING PROP. Meet day plays A DIFFERENT LIFTER than the one you just trained. useMeetDay calls newServerRecord on mount and builds the entire meet from it; AppShell gives SessionScreen a serverPort and gives MeetScreen NO PORT, NO RECORD, NO CACHE; and appSessionPort holds the app one server connection that useMeetDay never asks for. So in the shipped path, forever: bestE1rmKg is the signup seed, so every meet suggests the same three openers on day 1 and day 400; totalKg is null, so the recap says FIRST TOTAL every time; record.meets is empty, so isPrAttempt is permanently false and GDD §6.3 attempt tension - the thing the document itself calls THE REAL TENSION - IS DEAD CODE IN THE SHIPPED APP; and MEET_ALREADY_RECORDED, the guard against banking one meet twice, can never fire. THE REPO HAD ALREADY DIAGNOSED AND FIXED THIS EXACT DEFECT TWICE, in headers that argue the general case - it reached for the row, the connection belongs to the app not to a screen, the ternary is a full unmount - and the guard EXISTS: sessionWiring.test.ts bans six strings from useSession.ts as exactly what the bypass was made of, and useMeetDay.ts CONTAINS FIVE OF THEM plus the meet analogue of the sixth, with zero matching guards of its own. The sharpest detail: meetServer.ts comments on meetDayFacts that it is THE ONE PLACE A TRAINING NUMBER CROSSES INTO MEET DAY and makes that number unit compile-time provable - and the crossing does not happen, so the number is unit-proven and constant. The critic also showed the only recap screenshot ever taken showing COMPETITION PR is the FROZEN DEBUG PATH fed a fabricated 605kg history: the played app cannot produce that picture. Not one of the 94 browser checks compares a quantity on the two sides of the press that crosses modes. Builder out. || FIXED AND MERGED, 2644 GREEN, 102 BROWSER CHECKS. I opened the new shot and the bench opener reads 110, under copy that says Pre-filled from your training - true for the first time. THE REPRODUCTION COST TWO FINDINGS WORTH MORE THAN THE PLUMBING. The input-completeness control REFUSED TO RUN rather than passing over unreadable inputs, because the parser read STARTING_E1RM.deadlift as missing - it is the last entry of an inline object with no trailing comma. THE EQUALITY WOULD HAVE PASSED VACUOUSLY ON THE BROKEN BUILD; only the non-vacuity control made that visible. Structurally: the port is a required first parameter, the ban forbids the row-building names, MeetServerPort exposes none, and appSessionPort() === appMeetPort(). The preview ternary that was one branch doing two jobs is replaced by the preview server and its state being ONE VALUE, so they cannot disagree. meetDayFacts now takes a structural MeetDayHistory rather than a ServerRecord - that parameter type WAS the cause, since a client may not hold a row and so had to fabricate one to have something to pass. Ten mutations; the sharpest TYPECHECKS and hands the client the whole ServerRecord under a key nobody was watching. An EIGHTH instance of the guarantee pattern found in passing: appServer.ts cited a test file that does not exist. NEWLY REACHABLE AND FLAGGED: MEET_ALREADY_RECORDED fires on the second meet of an app run - correct, not a dead end, but the recap is blank with a way out, and the entry gate belongs to GDD §6.1 Career calendar. || PLACEHOLDER SHIPPED PER THE HUMAN RULING, 2651 GREEN, 103 BROWSER CHECKS. Reproduced first on real numbers: meet 1 banks 612.5kg under local-open-2026 and its recap builds, meet 2 reports the SAME id and is refused, so the beat stayed recap with no recap object and the screen fell through to a bare MEET COMPLETE eyebrow. The scaffolding test catches: the module imports only TYPES, so a file that imports no values cannot read a clock, a row or meet history; the export surface is exact BOTH ways; the view takes no props; both files carry a code-line ceiling; and the pin runs in both directions between the module and GDD §6.1. A NEW SHAPE OF THE VACUITY FAILURE, FOUND IN ITS OWN WORK: its first pin was SOURCE.includes(THE_CONSTANT) where the module declares that constant from a literal, so the file necessarily contains its own value and the assertion CANNOT FAIL - every previous instance in this codebase was prose without a test, this one is a test assertion that cannot fail, and the witness bar does not catch it because a witness proves ONE assertion bites rather than all of them. BROWSER LIMIT DISCLOSED: the positive case is NOT verified in a browser, because reaching the placeholder needs two whole meets in one page session and the rep is a genuine timing mechanic a scripted mouse does not beat reliably, so the committed check is the negative half only and the code says so. AWAITING A HUMAN: the copy says Meet recorded, and the meet just lifted was NOT recorded - it was refused, and the result on the row is the EARLIER meet. True of the row, arguably misleading about the nine attempts just taken. || COPY CORRECTED BY THE HUMAN. It now reads Meet complete - results saved to your last recorded meet. Career calendar coming soon. The builder shipping it unedited and flagging it rather than quietly changing it is what made the correction possible. THE SELF-REFERENTIAL ASSERTION IS FIXED AND I MUTATION-TESTED THE REPLACEMENT rather than taking the report word: removing the section citation from the module now reddens by name. AND VACUITY IS ITS OWN NAMED CATEGORY in CLAUDE.md now, separate from the prose-without-a-test rule, because they are different failure shapes needing different scans and they look identical in a green suite. The definition is stated so it can be applied - an assertion is vacuous if NO STATE of the code it is meant to be checking would make it red, not it-passes-today but there-is-no-version-of-the-subject-that-fails-it - with six shapes listed from this run own history: self-referential, an empty domain, a bound the unfixed behaviour already satisfied, an oracle mirroring its subject, a domain that cannot reach the case, and an input silently absent. || COHERENCE RE-GRADED ON THE FIXED ARTIFACT: the one-lifter seam IS CLOSED and the critic said so - appSessionPort() === appMeetPort() is the same object, useMeetDay has no way to build a record, and the browser record proves the CONSEQUENCE rather than the mechanism, with a control showing the seed would have given 107.5. But the bar still fails, on a different seam: THE SAME DayOpening MAPPING IS IMPLEMENTED TWICE AND THE TWO DISAGREE. sessionServer names three kinds including gap-covered-by-recovery-days; sessionClient names TWO, so that kind falls through to a literal 1 - and the correct twin todayForLifter has NO NON-TEST CALLER, so the client wrong answer is the app ONLY answer. I verified both sites and confirmed sessionServer is the only file outside streak.ts that names the missing kind. It reaches pixels: a lifter on a 10-day run who misses three days and returns sees 1 over DAY STREAK with the celebratory pop playing, then it snaps to 11 about 558ms later - LOCAL_SERVER_LATENCY_MS is 550 and the browser record measured the settle at 558, so this is half a second of on-screen wrong number on the beat GDD §4.3 calls THE PHEW BEAT, the one that exists to tell a player their streak was saved. WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: sessionClient.test.ts only ever builds states with lastTrainedDay set to yesterday, so the covered-gap case is NOT IN ITS DOMAIN - the empty-domain vacuity shape verbatim - nothing renders in the suite, and the 103 browser checks play a day-1 lifter where the fall-through to 1 is COINCIDENTALLY CORRECT. The critic also found the §4.3 reveal payload is computed correctly and DROPPED TWICE before anything can render it. Builder out on one mapping, an exhaustive switch, and a sweep with a non-vacuity guard over all seven kinds. || FIXED AND MERGED, 2654 GREEN. One exported mapping both callers render - not two pinned equal - with an exhaustive switch and a never fallthrough, and a sweep whose oracle is THE REAL RECORDER rather than a case analysis, over every 10-day calendar at every window balance with non-vacuity pinning COUNTS not bounds. M4 IS THE LOAD-BEARING MUTATION: putting the old ternary chain back reddens the client tests and LEAVES THE SWEEP GREEN, so a pure-logic sweep alone could never have caught this. A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE BEYOND THE BRIEF, FLAGGED NOT BURIED: day-in-past now carries currentStreak, forced by the oracle rather than taste, because recordTrainingDay REFUSES that day so the streak cannot move - and without the field the mapping was silently answering 1 there too, across 11,778 openings on runs longer than a day, reachable in the shipped app. THE SAME BLIND SPOT IN A THIRD PLACE: sessionPreview previewContext HARDCODES the value and never calls the mapping, so every debug session moment bypasses it - the yesterday-only fixture existed in the unit tests, the preview module AND the browser fixtures, three harnesses blind for one reason. It declined to add a browser check rather than ship an unexercised one. TWO THINGS I FOUND MYSELF. The timeout comment in vitest.config.ts named three heavy tests and NONE are in the top ten; measured and rewritten with real numbers, and the margin recorded - the two slowest sit at 56% of the 30s budget unloaded, and every one of the top six is in streakEntitlement.test.ts, which is why that file sets the wall. Re-run under pipefail; the first honest run FAILED INTERMITTENTLY on the placeholder negative check and three further runs passed 103/0, so that check is flaky and cannot be trusted to redden on a real regression either. || THE INTERVAL BETWEEN BORN AND ADMITTED IS CLOSED, BY REMOVING THE CAPABILITY RATHER THAN ENUMERATING ITS USES. Three lines at useSession.ts:276 wrote a pound e1RM into a wire with tsc clean and an identical test count - the bar itself failing with all four guards green. The builder measured what the reproduction actually DID, which nobody had: the poisoned number lands as confirmed 485.0 against a true 220kg, and IN THE BROWSER IT PRINTS 485.0 kg ON THE CLOSE-OUT. With the seal in place the same played session throws "Cannot assign to read only property" and the e1RM stays 220.0 - which settles strict-vs-sloppy in the SHIPPED BUNDLE, a question node alone could not answer. || THE MUTANT WORTH THE ROUND fired exactly where I warned it might: sealing a SHALLOW SPREAD and handing out the original left the reproduction test GREEN, because a spread shares its nested objects so the write still threw. Only a separate Object.isFrozen(wire) assertion caught it. || TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY BRIEF: I cited GDD 7.1 for the unit boundary and GDD 7.1 is ART DIRECTION - the 7.1 that matters is progression.ts's own internal numbering, and my brief inherited a bad reference. And I asserted freezing was not a hot path; the builder MEASURED it rather than agreeing - 20k calls, 0.45us to 3.68us, about 8x on functions called a handful of times per app run. Negligible, but now a number. || 2663 tests, tsc clean, 140 browser checks still green. || THE SEAL WAS DEFEATABLE AND IS NOW RESOLVED. A fresh critic found that isSealedAt matched its callee by identifier TEXT while the receive check TWELVE LINES BELOW IN THE SAME visit FUNCTION resolved symbols through the checker and followed aliases. Now fourteen mutants, run in BOTH directions at all seven sites - seal deleted and seal replaced by Object.freeze, the second half mattering because freeze is shallow. A namespace-import probe stays correctly green. || I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE FOUR SITES AND IT CHANGED THE WORK: two were module-private and one was unobservable through any public door, so the builder exported one and extracted another out of a ternary, renaming a 7.5 row. It also corrected my charge on an assertion - unreachably-red rather than vacuous. || MeetResultWire as a target is NOT mechanical, measured with a checker probe: four shipped literals, none the seal's first argument, one reached by dataflow through a named const, one not a wire at all, and RouteSite kind has no room for a fourth species. || LEDGER NOW BITES. Four files share md5 84e48be8 - 01, 05, 05a and 05b - but 05 PREDATES this wave, so only TWO of the four new shots are redundant. Re-hashed and confirmed; the correction is committed. Every press of the only control in the app costs two minutes and returns nothing, until the calendar rolls. The bar's letter is met - every surface has a drawn, hit-tested exit - and its spirit is met by a graph whose terminal component is two nodes and no progress. The critic named it correctly: not a dead end, not a clean deferral, a DISCARDED-PROGRESS LOOP. || AND THE TRANSITION IS EXERCISED NOWHERE. route.json's two player-path leave-meet presses land on a FRESH check-in, because no session had been played at that point in the run; the played-session section reaches already-trained, presses MEET DAY, checks the opener and STOPS. report.title: Where this actually is
report.lede: Recounted from the repo at HEAD. Suite 3312 across 83 files, typecheck clean. THE HEADLINE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT THIS RUN COULD TAKE: multiple people played the MVP and the squat is FUN. That is the first verdict in this build on the one bar no critic here could ever grade, and GDD §10's gate - "do not build Gym Empire before the lift mechanic is proven fun" - is open. It validates the core mechanic and nothing else; the crowd-reaction beat and the PR-attempt wording stay separate playtest questions. Two findings came back with it. An ENVIRONMENT defect, fixed: pressing on a mobile browser triggered the browser's own text-selection gesture, which is exactly the gesture a press-and-hold mechanic is built on. And a DESIGN question, deliberately left open: players were unclear how to perform the down-and-back-up motion. The two are entangled - some of "confusing" may have been people fighting the browser - so the fix landed first and the clarity complaint gets re-tested before anything is designed for it. Bench and deadlift are now justified rather than premature, and held until that re-test. Also landed: GDD §2.1's Career spine, built pure-logic-first, then sent back by a critic whose finding was better than the build it graded.

Higher risk." while isPrAttempt needs a previous best to beat — false for any big jump at or below the existing best, which is most openers and second attempts. Measured at 53 of 72 cards in the sweep and 4 non-PR big cards on the played second meet. Not the first-meet edge case it was reported as. || THE COUNTERFACTUAL RAN FIRST: replacing the gold PR border with null left the whole suite green at 66/2812 with tsc clean. The border had never had a check, and STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT HAVE BEEN DRAWN on any screen a player reaches — a first meet has no record to beat, so a PR attempt exists only on the second meet of one app run. || Fixed structurally: the sentence and the border are now filled from the SAME expression, so the screen cannot say PR while the border disagrees in either direction. The WORDS are a placeholder — two options are recorded in the GDD and a playtester picks between them, with overturning the shipped one named as a normal outcome.

rows.note: Built by the PARALLEL SESSION, sent back once for having no loop, rebuilt with one, and then found to PUNISH DAILY ENGAGEMENT - CLAUDE.md's absolute - in five pairs out of 16512. The no-gacha ban still wins its bar outright: 18 regexes over comment-stripped source, every one driven against a tripwire, scanned and banned.length both pinned. || THE FIVE WERE REAL AND THE STATED CAUSE WAS FALSE. Carried for several waves and written down four times - my brief, GDD §5.4, engagement.test.ts's header and the human ruling acting on all three - all saying the recruit price ladder: cost per unit rises across tiers, bestRecruitableTier takes the priciest affordable rung. Measured, it is false of every one of the five. The diligent gym takes a novice at 500 per unit and the idle gym takes a club at 1250, so the diligent gym buys the CHEAPER and MORE EFFICIENT rung and loses anyway. || WHAT THEY ACTUALLY WERE: a roster slot, once filled, was filled forever, and §5.3's ladder unlocks on reputation, which rises with the calendar. The diligent gym hits its last free slot at reputation 48.8 - club opens at 50 - and commits it to a novice; the idle gym hits the same slot six check-ins later at 59.2 and takes a club. Being early was the trap. Fixed with a promotion path, 5 to 0, and the promotion mechanic itself is now a question for a human because it is a NEW §5.3 rule added on a repair brief. || ONE ARM IS STILL NOT ZERO. spend-once-per-calendar-day gives 6459 of 8064 and the human has ruled it representative player behaviour rather than a control, so it is a live exposure. Its cause is proved, not asserted: hold the day's spending anchor at the less-engaged history's own and all 24576 pairs give 0 while 9731 still move.

groups.title: MVP — one loop playable end to end on a device — MET
groups.body: MET as of this commit, and verified on the running app rather than asserted. A player opens the app, does a daily session, enters a meet, completes it and comes back, without typing a URL: 47 of 47 checks pass, including PRESSING IT REACHES MEET DAY with no query string and FINISH A SESSION to REACH A MEET in one press. The estimate was 1 build plus 1 to 2 reworks at high confidence; it took 1 build and 0 reworks, which is the fastest any piece has landed in this run. Two caveats stated rather than buried: 6.1 Career gating is not built, so there is one ungated door to one local meet; and the already-trained-today surface is unit-tested but has no rendered frame, which is the one place the never-punish argument would want pixels.

groups.title: Alpha — four modes present, math and rules bars won
groups.body: The math half is effectively there: five of six lifting-math and rules pieces have won. The mode half is not — three of the four modes are zero files. Estimate: roughly 12 to 18 rounds. Basis, from this run: a piece from nothing to a won bar has cost 4 to 6 rounds (M1 six, M4 five, S2 five so far, A1 five and still unmet), and three unbuilt modes plus cut-ins is four pieces. MEDIUM CONFIDENCE on the arithmetic, LOW on the total, because every mode built so far surfaced gaps in pieces that were already called done — the S2 venue work broke A2 palette assumptions, and A1 shading broke A2 negative controls.

groups.title: Beta — art bars won where gradeable, tuning set by playtesting
groups.body: NOT REACHABLE FROM INSIDE THIS RUN, and that is a fact about the environment rather than an estimate. GDD §12.1 budgets roughly 30 hand-tuning iterations by actual playtesting, and every walkout duration, judging threshold, crowd rise, haptic pattern and sound recipe is currently an unplayed placeholder that says so in its own header. No critic can substitute for that — CLAUDE.md is explicit. The rounds I can still spend usefully are the ones that make values tunable and honest, not the ones that set them.

groups.title: Permanently unverifiable here, and why
groups.body: Three bars cannot be settled in this environment no matter how many rounds are spent. The 16-bit era A/B for gym art: docs/reference/README.md records that no gym-interior reference is committed, and image hosts return 403 by policy. Meet-day pacing and sound: broadcast footage is unreachable, WebFetch returns markdown rather than pixels or audio, and nothing here can capture sound. Result-card typography: four separate critics confirmed the 403s themselves rather than inheriting the claim. In each case the honest outcome is the one taken — the artifact is built to be tunable and the bar is reported unverifiable rather than passed on argument.

groups.title: What the count means, and why it will grow again
groups.body: Seven of twenty-two is the strict reading: won means a critic passed it with no open gap. Six more (M2, M3, M4, A2 and others above) are majority-passes where everything gradeable was met and the residue is either awaiting a human ruling or is permanently unverifiable. The denominator is pieces DEFINED SO FAR and has grown twice: the licensing architecture did not exist as a piece two days ago, the app shell was invisible until this recount, and cut-ins have had a GDD bar all along with nobody assigned. Twenty-four checks that could not fail have been found so far, and each new piece has surfaced more; the realistic expectation is that Y keeps rising as the remaining modes expose gaps in pieces currently called done.
